correctness.rationale: In a zero-adjoined abelian group, two products agree either because both supports meet the absorbing element, or because all union variables are group-valued and an integer linear map vanishes. The first has probability \(1-s^i-s^j+s^u\), the second \(s^u/|dG|\) by the finite homomorphism fiber theorem and Bezout. Every support triple and divisor is attained. Exact monotonicity establishes the global minimum and its equality cases; explicit distinct sequences and a compactness argument establish the three derived sets; a finite five-adic valuation proof separates \(C_4^0\) and \((C_2\times C_2)^0\). Two independent exhaustive small-word checkers agree (25,269 plus 8,428 equations); no infinite theorem is inferred from tests.

value.rationale: Determines a complete natural word-equation invariant for every finite abelian group with absorbing zero, a class sitting outside the minimal-spectrum regime of a contemporary research program. It identifies the entire topological accumulation hierarchy, proves the sharp least probability with all equality cases, and uses an exact nonmembership proof to distinguish same-order nonisomorphic group parts (\(C_4\) and \(C_2\times C_2\)). These structural facts are not merely a numerical check or relabeling.
